speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing a psychiatric condition along with a new movement disorder; to begin our assessment, could you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and what specific movements are you noticing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; the timing of your movement disorder appearing two months after starting risperidone is significant. Have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or involuntary movements in your face or limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Acute Dystonia (likely Akathisia based on symptoms).

You describe an inability to remain still with restlessness and fidgeting, which are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I need to see a physical exam of your muscle tone and check your vital signs. REQUEST TEST: Vitals (Heart Rate, Blood Pressure).
